title: CacheRepair: Learning to Repair Cross-Chunk Context in RAG for KV Cache Fusion
summary: CacheRepair replaces full joint prefill over retrieved chunks (and expensive selective recomputation) with independent per-chunk KV precomputation plus a small learned network that predicts residuals restoring cross-chunk context. The cost is a per-target-LLM training run of the repair network on a retrieval corpus, online cache transfer plus repair latency already included in TTFT, and added serving complexity. It can fail when the frozen target LLM or retrieval distribution changes (requiring retraining), and quality gains were not uniform across all model-dataset pairs, so small repairers may recover less cross-chunk context than reported best cases.
rationale: The method is deployable on a single GPU with a frozen LLM and a small trained repairer, but its quality-latency benefit depends on the reader's specific model and retrieval workload, so a workload-specific pilot is warranted before adoption.
technique: Learned repair of independently precomputed RAG KV caches

claims.statement: CacheRepair replaces full joint prefill over retrieved chunks (and expensive selective recomputation) with independent per-chunk KV precomputation plus a small learned network that predicts residuals restoring cross-chunk context. The cost is a per-target-LLM training run of the repair network on a retrieval corpus, online cache transfer plus repair latency already included in TTFT, and added serving complexity. It can fail when the frozen target LLM or retrieval distribution changes (requiring retraining), and quality gains were not uniform across all model-dataset pairs, so small repairers may recover less cross-chunk context than reported best cases.
Largest repairers achieve 1.69-4.61x speedups in median TTFT over full prefill and improve mean F1 by 2.1-26.1 percentage points over direct cache reuse, across three LLMs and four datasets.
